page: Microsoft Azure D8plds_v5 is an ARM-based compute instance built on the Ampere Altra ARMv8 architecture utilizing Neoverse-N1 cores. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per core running at 3.0 GHz, supported by 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache pool. The configuration is provisioned with 16.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 322 GB of local SSD temporary storage and supports Azure Premium Storage, operating without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluation reveals consistent multi-threaded scale alongside modest single-core throughput. The instance achieves average mid-tier results in stress-ng tests (1,822.9 single-core and 14,501.82 multi-core) and Geekbench multi-core performance (6,013.0). In contrast, Geekbench single-core output (1,057.0) and PassMark CPU metrics (6,130.18) register in the lower quartile, reflecting the baseline per-core execution speeds typical of Neoverse-N1 implementations. The system demonstrates reliable throughput in software compilation with Clang (9,351.0) and static web serving (9.92 GB/sec), while data decompression and image processing workloads reflect architecture-level bottlenecks.

Memory bandwidth tests indicate 84.32 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 43.64 GB/sec for uncached writes, delivering adequate support for standard application buffers despite an overall low PassMark memory score of 1,635.6. Real-world key-value tests show solid throughput, executing 10.26 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining balanced mid-range performance in PassMark database operations (5,456.36). Natural language processing workloads remain a clear tradeoff; LLM inference rates are constrained, producing 44.93 tokens/sec on small models (135M) and dropping to 7.58 tokens/sec on 7B parameter models.

The 1:2 memory ratio and physical-core mapping make the D8plds_v5 a cost-effective choice for scale-out microservices, CI/CD code compilation pipelines, network routing layers, and compute-dense workloads that prioritize dedicated core counts over large memory footings. Workloads requiring x86 instruction sets (AVX-512, AMX), extensive vector mathematics, or high memory per core are better directed to alternative instance families.
description: Microsoft Azure D8plds_v5 is an ARM64 virtual machine powered by Ampere Neoverse-N1 processors running at 3.0 GHz across 8 dedicated vCPUs. Configured in a compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it supplies 16.0 GB of RAM alongside 322 GB of integrated local SSD storage. Multi-threaded benchmark testing reflects stable middle-tier performance, including 14,501.82 in stress-ng multi-core and 10.26 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. However, single-core execution speeds and vector-intensive processes represent noticeable tradeoffs, showing lower-quartile results across Geekbench single-core, bzip3 decompression, and LLM text generation. With dedicated cores and integrated local disk space, the D8plds_v5 offers solid operational efficiency for software build pipelines, web serving clusters, and containerized scale-out microservices.
